Steps.1: Review the schematic design of the hw_DAA. Check that the RS485 transceiver has flow control signals to avoid the echo reading.
Steps.2: Connect the hw_DAA to a PC. Set up the FPGA to pull data through the RS485 signals (TX & RX).
Steps.3: Connect the hw_DAA to a DAA CS harness.
Steps.4: Connect the power supply to the DAA CS harness power input, using a DC power connector, banana cables, and crocodile clips (according to the attached diagram).
Steps.5: Switch on the power supply source.
Steps.6: Set 12V and 3A on the CH1 of the power supply source.
Steps.7: Turn on the CH1 of the power supply source.
Steps.9: Connect on CH1 an oscilloscope probe to UART_0_TX signal (pin 5 of the IC25) with x10 attenuation.
Steps.10: Connect on CH2 an oscilloscope probe to UART_0_RX signal (pin 2 of the IC25) with x10 attenuation.
Steps.11: Connect on CH3 an oscilloscope probe to RS485_DE signal (pin 4 of the IC25) with x10 attenuation.
Steps.12: Connect on CH4 an oscilloscope probe to !RS485_RE signal (pin 3 of the IC25) with x10 attenuation.
Steps.13: Set the vertical grid to 500 mV/div on all the channels. Set the vertical offset to -1V.
Steps.14: Set the horizontal grid to ~2 us/div and center the horizontal trigger position around the center of the oscilloscope screen.
Steps.15: Ensure that the attenuation is set to x10 and BW limit OFF on all the channels.
Steps.16: Set the trigger level to ~2V, rising edge and source the CH1.
Steps.17: Click on the Single button to capture communication frames of the RS485.
Steps.18: Check that when the RS485 is transmitting data (CH1), the voltage at RS485_DE and !RS485_RE signals (CH3 & CH4) is 3.3V.
Steps.19: Take an oscilloscope screenshot (with and without zoom).
Steps.20: Check that when the RS485 is receiving data (CH2), the voltage at RS485_DE and !RS485_RE signals (CH3 & CH4) is 0V.
Steps.21: Take an oscilloscope screenshot (with and without zoom).
